record.paper_title: PURE O-SEQUENCES: KNOWN RESULTS, APPLICATIONS AND OPEN PROBLEMS
record.original_question: Determine the smallest number n of variables for which there exists a nonunimodal pure f-vector, equivalently a nonunimodal f-vector of a pure simplicial complex. The paper notes this after recalling Stanley's original nonunimodal example and later bounds for special cases.

evidence.quote: What is the smallest number of variables n (i.e., the number of vertices of the complex) allowing the existence of a nonunimodal pure f-vector?

A. Tahat [76] has recently determined the sharp lower bound n = 328 for nonuni- modal Cohen-Macaulay f-vectors of socle degree 5 (the socle degree of Stanley’s original example), and has produced examples in larger socle degree with n as low as 39.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A simplicial complex Δ on a finite vertex set V is called pure if all of its facets (maximal faces under inclusion) have the same dimension. Its f-vector is f(Δ) = (f₋₁, f₀, f₁, …, f_{d−1}), where f_i is the number of i-dimensional faces of Δ (with f₋₁ = 1 for the empty face). The f-vector is called unimodal if there exists an index j such that f₋₁ ≤ f₀ ≤ ⋯ ≤ f_j ≥ f_{j+1} ≥ ⋯ ≥ f_{d−1}; otherwise it is called nonunimodal.

Determine the smallest positive integer n with the following property: there exists a pure simplicial complex Δ on n vertices whose f-vector is nonunimodal. Equivalently, find the minimum number of vertices required to support a nonunimodal pure f-vector.
artifact.status_search_result: The exact minimum number of vertices needed for a pure simplicial complex to admit a nonunimodal f-vector does not appear to be known. Partial results exist: a sharp lower bound of n = 328 has been established for nonunimodal Cohen–Macaulay f-vectors of socle degree 5, with examples in higher socle degree using as few as n = 39 vertices, but no general sharp bound for arbitrary pure complexes has been confirmed in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: f-vectors of pure complexes and pure multicomplexes of rank three
status_evidence.snippet: Studies pure complexes and the unimodality question for low rank, leaving the minimum-vertex case for general nonunimodality unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: Work on pure complex f-vectors discusses unimodality but does not pin down the smallest n admitting nonunimodal pure f-vectors.

status_evidence.title: Stanley's work on unimodality
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of Stanley's nonunimodality examples and follow-up bounds.
status_evidence.claim: Original Stanley nonunimodal examples and subsequent improvements are recorded but no minimal-vertex value is established.
